4. MOS 0914, Marine Special Operations Forces Instructor (MGySgt to Sgt)
NMOS (0211, 0231, 0241, 0261, 0291, 0370, 0372 0411, 0431, 0451, 0481, 0491,
0621, 0627, 0629, 0631, 0639, 0671, 0679, 0681, 0699, 0861, 1141, 1142, 1341,
2111, 2171, 2311, 2336, 2621, 2629, 2631, 2641, 2651, 2659, 2691, 2831, 2841,
2847, 2862, 2891, 3043, 3051), DC PP&O

    a. Summary. Marine Special Operations Forces Instructors train and
certify Marines in entry level or advanced special operations skills. They
serve as mentors and coaches, assisting student in the development of problem
solving, critical thinking, and cognitive abilities for adaptive decision
making. They enable students to master the skills necessary to conduct
globally sensitive missions in complex environments.

       b.   Prerequisites

            (1) Must be a sergeant or above.

            (2) Mastery of the Marine’s PMOS.




                                          3-92                          Enclosure (1)
 3115                                                                  NAVMC 1200.1L



            (3) Must maintain the USMC standards for PFT and CFT for their PMOS.

        (4) Must meet Marine Corps height, weight, and body composition
standards.

        (5) Must meet the prerequisites prescribed in MCO 1553.2C Marine
Corps Formal School Management Policy.

        (6) Must meet the standards screening checklist of special
assignments per MCO 1326.6 Selecting, Screening and Preparing Enlisted
Marines for billets and independent duty assignments.

        (7) Must possess one of the following primary military occupational
specialties (PMOS) 0211, 0231, 0241, 0261, 0372, 0621, 0629, 0631, 0639,
0671, 0679, 0699, 2336, 2629, 2651, 2691, or 2841.

        (8) Successful completion of the Special Operations Training Course
(M03DTZK), Survival, Evasion, Resistance, Escape Level C Course (M03M47K),
and MARSOC Special Operations Force (SOF) Level 1 Training.

       c.   Requirements

        (1) Must successfully complete the MARSOC Instructor Qualification
Course (MO3YEQK) at the Marine Raider Training Center (MRTC) in Camp Lejeune,
NC.

            (2) Must be appointed in writing as a MRTC Instructor.

       d.   Duties

        (1) Trains personnel in entry level and/or advanced special
operations skills.

        (2) Responsible for the conduct and supervision of high risk
training.

    e. Related Standard Occupational Classification (SOC) Title and Code.
Teachers and Instructors, All other 25-3099.

       f.   Related Military Skill.   None.

Occupational Field 09, Training, comprises MOSs used to identify Marines who possess skill sets to conduct vital training, particularly to entry-level Marines, as required by various high visibility Marine Corps programs. First exposure to Marine Corps training is provided by the Drill Instructor. Next contact is with the marksmanship coaches and instructors overseen by a Range Officer, Swim Instructors, Martial Arts Instructors, and then Marine Combat Instructors. In the operating forces, training continues with the addition of Small Weapons Instructors and Martial Arts Instructor-Trainers. These MOSs are sponsored by the Training and Education Command.

4. MOS 0914, Marine Special Operations Forces Instructor (MGySgt to Sgt) NMOS (0211, 0231, 0241, 0261, 0291, 0370, 0372 0411, 0431, 0451, 0481, 0491, 0621, 0627, 0629, 0631, 0639, 0671, 0679, 0681, 0699, 0861, 1141, 1142, 1341, 2111, 2171, 2311, 2336, 2621, 2629, 2631, 2641, 2651, 2659, 2691, 2831, 2841, 2847, 2862, 2891, 3043, 3051), DC PP&O a. Summary. Marine Special Operations Forces Instructors train and certify Marines in entry level or advanced special operations skills. They serve as mentors and coaches, assisting student in the development of problem solving, critical thinking, and cognitive abilities for adaptive decision making. They enable students to master the skills necessary to conduct globally sensitive missions in complex environments. b. Prerequisites (1) Must be a sergeant or above. (2) Mastery of the Marine’s PMOS. (3) Must maintain the USMC standards for PFT and CFT for their PMOS. (4) Must meet Marine Corps height, weight, and body composition standards. (5) Must meet the prerequisites prescribed in MCO 1553.2C Marine Corps Formal School Management Policy. (6) Must meet the standards screening checklist of special assignments per MCO 1326.6 Selecting, Screening and Preparing Enlisted Marines for billets and independent duty assignments. (7) Must possess one of the following primary military occupational specialties (PMOS) 0211, 0231, 0241, 0261, 0372, 0621, 0629, 0631, 0639, 0671, 0679, 0699, 2336, 2629, 2651, 2691, or 2841. (8) Successful completion of the Special Operations Training Course (M03DTZK), Survival, Evasion, Resistance, Escape Level C Course (M03M47K), and MARSOC Special Operations Force (SOF) Level 1 Training. c. (2) Must be appointed in writing as a MRTC Instructor. d. Duties (1) Trains personnel in entry level and/or advanced special operations skills. nlx_method: NLx employer-demand profiles; private-only ownership unverified. Six-digit profiles pool specialty weighted task incidences after the existing review exclusion mask and five-job task-support floor; destination SOCs require 200 postings and nonzero tasks. Military profiles use binary accepted task presence and the same NLx reference RCA weights as civilian profiles: reciprocal positive task shares (zero weight for reference-absent tasks) of pooled retained support-five NLx weighted incidences across 1,016 reference specialties (912 eligible comparison candidates), sqrt(q * rca_weight), then L2 normalization and cosine. No military crosswalk codes enter the task ranking. All positive top-20 results retained; zero-similarity destinations are not recommendations. Shared field/rating duties are included; general Naval Standards remain separate by paygrade. Summary compares non-future individual source entries (versions can repeat) with nonempty reference sets; grouped, future and general-standard entries remain in all outputs. Hit@k is the fraction with at least one reference SOC recovered; ties are averaged exactly. References outside NLx remain in denominators. DMDC reference status is from July 2024, not current 2026 status.
